title: US considers lifting sanctions on some Iranian oil
byline: The US is weighing lifting sanctions on some Iranian oil, as it scrambles to contain the impact of its war in Iran on energy markets.

title: Missile lands next to presenter during live report from Lebanon
byline: Footage from Russian state broadcaster RT has captured the moment a missile lands just a few feet from where its reporter was broadcasting in southern Lebanon.

title: Oil storage complex abandoned
byline: A massive fuel storage complex near Thalawakele Railway Station for storing diesel and kerosene has been left to the mercy of the jungle for several decades.

title: Heavy social media use linked to falling youth happiness: Report
byline: The World Happiness Report 2026 has flagged serious concerns about how social media is affecting young people’s wellbeing around the world.

title: Sri Lanka lacks storage facilities for excess fuel shipments for April
byline: While long queues are still witnessed in most parts of the country, Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) sources yesterday said that while all fuel shipments ordered for April have been confirmed, Sri Lanka is facing a severe shortage of storage facilities to store the fuel and may not be able to place any further orders.

title: Meta will pay TikTokers and YouTubers up to $3,000 for Facebook posts
byline: Meta has launched a Creator Fast Track program to lure creators from TikTok, YouTube, and Instagram to Facebook, promising participants three months of fixed payouts, additional reach for Reels, and faster access to monetization.

title: Supreme Court rules foreign divorces must meet local law
byline: In a significant ruling, the Supreme Court of Sri Lanka has held that the recognition of a foreign judgement granting a divorce in Sri Lanka must strictly comply with domestic statutory provisions, thereby limiting the grounds for divorce to adultery after marriage, malicious desertion, or incurable impotence at the time of marriage.

title: Teenager among first to be executed over Iran’s anti-government protests
byline: Iran has executed three men accused of killing police officers during anti-government protests in January, state media say, the first hangings to be carried out in relation to the demonstrations.

title: Blasts heard over Jerusalem as Israel confirms strike on Iran gas field
byline: Explosions were heard over Jerusalem as fresh strikes were reported in Iran’s capital, Tehran, amid rapidly escalating tensions in the region. Iranian state television said at least four waves of missiles were launched in quick succession, signaling a sharp intensification of hostilities.

title: Tourist arrivals drop 18% in early March as transit disruptions bite
byline: Following a historic start to the year, Sri Lanka’s tourism sector is experiencing a notable deceleration, recording a steep 18.4 percent drop in international visitors during the first half of March 2026, a

title: Govt needs facts, not praise: Deputy Media Minister
byline: Deputy Minister of Mass Media Dr. Kaushalya Ariyaratne has called on both mainstream and social media to report the country’s current situation responsibly, said that the government does not require praise but expects accurate and factual reporting.

title: PHIs warn of service disruptions over fuel access issues
byline: Public Health Inspectors (PHIs) have raised serious concerns over difficulties in obtaining fuel for official duties, warning that essential public health services could be disrupted if immediate solutions are not provided.

title: Sri Lanka refused US request to land two fighter jets in Mattala: President
byline: Sri Lanka refused the request by three Iranian ships to come to Sri Lanka on a goodwill visit and the request by the United States to land its two fighter jets  in Mattala, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told Parliament today.

title: Sri Lanka ready to welcome and support refugees from India: Minister Bimal Rathnayake
byline: Sri Lanka is ready to receive and support all those forced to flee the country during the civil war and now living as refugees in Tamil Nadu, Cabinet Minister and Leader of the House Bimal Rathnayake told The Hindu, urging the Governments of India and Tamil Nadu to refrain from using refugees as “a tool for political propaganda”.

title: President addresses Parliament
byline: President Anura Kumara Dissanayake is currently addressing Parliament, providing an update on the state of the nation and the ongoing international developments.

title: Over 2,000 went missing during final stages of Sri Lankan civil war: Minister
byline: Some 2,764 persons have gone missing during the final stages of the civil war in 2009, but it is debatable, Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara told Parliament today.

title: Court orders Bribery Commission to record statement from Duminda Silva
byline: Colombo Magistrate Asanga S. Bodaragama today directed the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption to record a statement from former parliamentarian Duminda Silva, who is currently on death row, on March 23 at 10 a.m.

title: Trump 24-karat gold coin approved by hand-picked federal panel
byline: A commemorative gold coin bearing the image of US President Donald Trump has been approved by a federal arts commission.

title: Sri Lanka economy stable but vulnerable to global shocks: IMF
byline: The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has confirmed that it will conduct a combined fifth and sixth review of Sri Lanka’s Extended Fund Facility (EFF) during an upcoming mission to Colombo, scheduled from March 26 to April 9, 2026.

title: Uproar in Parliament after Minister shows middle finger to Opposition MP
byline: Parliament went into chaos after Minister of Justice Harshana Nanayakkara showed his middle finger to MP Ajith P. Perera who raised an oral question.

title: Iran hits Kuwaiti oil refinery as Israel renews attacks on Tehran
byline: Drones have struck Kuwait’s largest oil refinery for the second day as Iran launched a sweeping assault on energy infrastructure across the Gulf, while explosions boomed over Tehran from Israeli attacks as the country marked the Persian New Year.

title: CPC assures weekend fuel supply, denies closure rumors
byline: The Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) siad that fuel distribution to dealers will continue uninterrupted tomorrow and the day after, despite circulating rumors of a potential shutdown.

title: Lanka Sathosa launches nationwide New Year discount drive with up to 40% off essentials
byline: A special islandwide sales promotion campaign offering discounts of up to 40% on essential goods was launched today (20) by Lanka Sathosa, targeting relief for consumers ahead of the Sinhala and Hindu New Year season.

title: Ravi K raises concerns on air transport, airport capacity
byline: UNP MP Ravi Karunanayake raised a series of questions in Parliament seeking clarity on the current state of Sri Lanka’s aviation sector, including airline operations, passenger volumes, airport capacity, and the collection of embarkation taxes.

title: IRGC spokesman killed in strike, Iran says
byline: The spokesperson for Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, Ali Mohammad Naini, has been killed in strikes launched by the US and Israel, Iranian state media reports.

title: Chuck Norris, film star and martial artist, dies aged 86
byline: Actor and martial artist Chuck Norris, known for his roles in Way Of The Dragon and Missing In Action, has died after a sudden hospitalisation.

title: CSE extends gains as positive sentiment lifts indices on favorable market developments
byline: The Colombo Stock Exchange continued its recovery momentum on 20th March 2026, as improved investor sentiment supported a strong upward movement throughout the session. The market maintained a steady positive trajectory from the opening bell, driven by renewed confidence following recent volatility, with the ASPI recording a notable gain of 375.72 points by the close.

title: SLC makes fitness test mandatory for IPL 2026 NOCs
byline: Sri Lanka Cricket (SLC) has announced that players seeking to participate in the 2026 Indian Premier League (IPL) will only be granted No Objection Certificates (NOCs) upon successfully passing the board’s mandatory Physical Performance Test.

title: Teenage daughter of North Korean leader Kim Jong-un drives tank at military drill
byline: The teenage daughter of North Korea’s leader Kim Jong-un was seen driving a tank alongside her father during a military training exercise, adding to speculation that she is being groomed as his successor.

title: Systematic fuel supply mechanism planned for container trucks
byline: A systematic procedure is being prepared to ensure an adequate fuel supply for container trucks, as part of efforts to ease congestion at the Colombo Port and maintain the smooth flow of imports and exports.

title: FIFA fines Israeli FA for anti-discrimination rules breaches
byline: FIFA fined the Israeli Football Association (IFA) 150,000 Swiss francs ($190,700) on Thursday for ’’multiple breaches’’ of its anti-discrimination obligations.

title: Cabinet Committee meets to ensure uninterrupted public service
byline: The first meeting of the Cabinet Committee appointed to ensure the continuity and systematic functioning of the public service was held yesterday (19) at the Presidential Secretariat under the patronage of Prime Minister Harini Amarasuriya.
